providers.name: Nominatim
providers.policy: Maximum 1 request per second and an identifying User-Agent - both enforced here.

providers.name: Overpass API
providers.role: map features (roads, water, land use) as GeoJSON
providers.policy: Shared public instance: queries are radius-capped and cached rather than streamed per pan.

providers.name: OSM raster tiles
providers.policy: OpenStreetMap tile servers are donated capacity: they are for interactive use at a human pace, not for bulk download or prefetching a whole AOI.

basemaps.label: OSM Street
basemaps.note: The reference OpenStreetMap raster style. Volunteer-mapped, so detail varies by region.

basemaps.label: OSM Humanitarian
basemaps.attribution: © OpenStreetMap contributors, Tiles: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team
basemaps.note: HOT styling emphasises roads, tracks, settlements and water - useful for rural access planning.

basemaps.label: OSM Terrain
basemaps.note: Contour lines and hillshade on top of OpenStreetMap data - the drainage read, not the crop read.

feature_kinds.label: Roads and tracks
feature_kinds.note: Every highway class, including farm tracks (highway=track) and service ways.

feature_kinds.label: Waterways and ditches
feature_kinds.note: Drains, ditches, canals and streams - the lines that decide where water leaves a field.

feature_kinds.label: Land use
feature_kinds.note: Includes farmland, meadow, orchard, forest and industrial ground - the field's real neighbours.

feature_kinds.label: Buildings and yards
feature_kinds.note: Farm buildings, sheds and tanks - useful for yard and access planning.

feature_kinds.label: Hedges and fences
feature_kinds.note: Mapped hedgerows and fences. Real fields are often unbounded in OSM, so absence here means unmapped, not absent.

note: A 5xx from a provider is retried once after a pause; a 429 is never retried, because that is the provider asking us to slow down. All OpenStreetMap access is server-side: the browser talks only to this API, which spaces requests to the public per-second policy, caches replies, and reports the attribution and licence the map must carry. Data is © OpenStreetMap contributors under ODbL 1.0 - attribution is a licence condition, not a courtesy.
